decision.rationale: Cycle 6 fixes per-scope lifecycle reference status, and configured checks pass. Approval remains withheld because realistic recovery still conflicts with the immutable aggregate (PRR-003), and cleanup failure is discarded when choosing the attempt terminal state (PRR-004).

summary: Cycle 6 makes the direct mixed-outcome executor reach terminal evidence, but the committed replay test uses a constant application record unlike production and omits the crash-after-aggregate window. A realistic replay raises ROLLBACK_CLEANUP_REPLAY_CONFLICT. Separately, active oracle projection causes the controller to record ROLLED_BACK when authoritative terminal evidence says ROLLBACK_FAILED. Two S2 blockers remain.

findings.title: Cleanup failure is discarded when selecting the attempt terminal state
findings.observation: The active rollback oracle resolves authoritative terminal evidence and returns its reason and digest, but projection.rollback contains only the strict application rollback. recoverDeploymentFailure derives ROLLED_BACK versus ROLLBACK_FAILED solely from projection.rollback.status.
findings.trigger: Application rollback is PASS or NOT_APPLICABLE while production or restore cleanup is FAIL, so terminal evidence is ROLLBACK_FAILED but the projected application status is non-failing.
findings.impact: The durable deployment attempt says ROLLED_BACK even though authoritative cleanup and terminal evidence say ROLLBACK_FAILED. Operators and later lifecycle steps receive a false success terminal state while owned resources may remain.

evidence.description: A temporary exact-head controller regression returned the cleanup-failed terminal reason with application NOT_APPLICABLE and expected ROLLBACK_FAILED; the controller produced ROLLED_BACK. The temporary edit was removed and the worktree returned clean.
The oracle returns terminal reason/digest but projects only applicationRollback, and the controller branches only on that projection's status.
A fresh-context independent review confirmed the closed control-flow contradiction and that it is distinct from the per-scope reference defect.

findings.remediation: Propagate and verify the authoritative terminal rollback state through the active-oracle/controller contract. The controller must not infer aggregate cleanup success from applicationRollback.status alone.
findings.verification: Add a full-controller recovery regression where application rollback is NOT_APPLICABLE or PASS and one cleanup scope fails. Require currentState ROLLBACK_FAILED, reason and evidence digest bound to terminal rollback evidence, with no success projection contradiction.

findings.title: Mixed cleanup recovery still conflicts with the durable aggregate
findings.observation: Cycle 6 correctly gives each applicable scope a status-compatible reference. Replay comparison, however, preserves only aggregate startedAt and finishedAt. executeRollbackWithCleanup reruns application rollback before consulting existing aggregate authority, and production rollback timestamps are volatile. After an aggregate-write crash, recomputing already-completed production cleanup can also change PASS to FAIL because the deleted resource set and database proof cannot be reconstructed.
findings.trigger: Retry the same rollback after aggregate persistence, either after full lifecycle finalization with a newly timestamped application rollback result or after a crash before production lifecycle CLEANED is persisted.
findings.impact: Recovery raises ROLLBACK_CLEANUP_REPLAY_CONFLICT before terminal completion. In the crash window, production can remain QUIESCING with resources already removed and terminal-rollback-evidence.json absent, preventing the required durable ROLLBACK_FAILED closure.

evidence.description: The committed mixed-result replay passed only with a constant application object. A temporary exact-head variant changed only its timestamps on the second invocation and failed at persistRollbackCleanupEvidence with ROLLBACK_CLEANUP_REPLAY_CONFLICT. The temporary test was removed and the worktree returned clean.

rollbackApplication generates new startedAt/finishedAt values, executeRollbackWithCleanup invokes it before aggregate resolution, and aggregate equality includes applicationRollbackSha256 plus both scoped results.
Fresh-context review additionally traced the aggregate-write-before-lifecycle crash window: retry cannot reconstruct production database proof and changes the durable production PASS result.
The design requires completed cleanup replay to return the same authority, and the Cycle 5 remediation verification explicitly requires replay without another delete or aggregate conflict.

findings.remediation: Resolve and reuse an existing exact aggregate or terminal authority before rerunning volatile application rollback or reconstructing already-consumed production cleanup proof. Resume missing lifecycle/terminal writes from the persisted scoped results and reject only genuine semantic conflicts.
findings.verification: Add crash injection immediately after aggregate persistence and replay with changed application timestamps. Require no second application or Docker side effect, production CLEANED, restore CLEANUP_FAILED, unchanged aggregate bytes, and terminal ROLLBACK_FAILED. Preserve the symmetric mixed-result case.
